items.title: Steve Angrum Interview, 1961-08-08
items.q: The interviewee does not mention Norey Dutre; the name is introduced solely by the interviewer as a relative of Hader.

ctx.x: I never did hear too much of him either, but I used to see him around that time. Yeah. Good kind of thing. Did you ever come across where Hader played the old Sam Lutre, Sam Lutre Sr.? Yeah, I don't know. I played with him. I played with him a couple times, you know. Yeah. Two clarinetes and a band? No, no. He played a ton of sax. Oh, yeah. And clarinet. Is that the old man or the young man that's living now? No, the young one. The young one was living now.

Well, yeah, but his father is supposed to be a clarinetist, too. Yeah. And his uncle, Norey Dutre, was a trombonist of Oliver. They were back in that period. Yeah. Well, I don't know where Norey is. I don't know where they're going to play. I was wondering about a couple of the other clarinetes that I missed, what they were like, for instance. Zeb. Zeb, yeah. You remember Zeb? Zeb, yeah. You ever hear him? Yeah.

What's his name? What's his second name? Do you know? Well, that's all I know is Zeb, Zeb, Zeb, yeah. And another good kind of clarinetes, too. Pills. Now, that's a relation to Zeb. Pills? Pills, yeah. That's a cripple fellow. He had one leg short enough.
